schema.definition: Defined dialectically by Socrates at Meno 76a7 as 'the limit of solid' (στερεοῦ πέρας), anticipating Euclid Elements I, Defs. 13–14 and XI, Def. 2.

stereon.loci: Meno 76a; Theaetetus 148b; Republic VII 528a–d; Timaeus 32b; Laws VII 817e
stereon.definition: Magnitude possessing depth (βάθος) in addition to length and breadth; requires two geometric means for continuous proportion (Timaeus 32b; Elements VIII.12).

epipedon.definition: Two-dimensional surface or plane product of two factors; joined in continuous proportion by a single mean proportional (Timaeus 32a; Elements VIII.11).

peras.definition: In Meno 76a, the bounding extremity of a magnitude; in Philebus 25a–d, the supreme ontological genus of equal, double, and every exact ratio of number to number or measure to measure that brings indeterminate continua into symmetry.

apeiron.definition: The domain of 'the more and less' (τὸ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον) lacking intrinsic numeric or geometric measure prior to the imposition of Limit (peras).

anamnesis.definition: Plato's epistemological thesis that geometric discovery—exemplified when Meno's untutored attendant recognizes Q = 4 + 4 = 8 from the diagonal diagram—consists in recovering necessary truths latent within rational soul.

diametros.translation: Diagonal of a square or diameter of a circle
diametros.definition: Technical geometric term ('as the sophists/geometers call it', Meno 85b4) for the line cutting a square into two equal isosceles right triangles, whose square has double the area of the original square.

hypothesis.definition: Both the geometer's analytic reduction of a problem to an auxiliary condition (Meno 86e–87a) and the unexamined postulates of odd, even, figures, and angles from which dianoia reasons downward (Republic VI 510c).

parateinein.definition: To apply (παρατείνειν) a given area along the diameter of a circle so as to fall short (ἐλλείπειν) by a figure similar to the applied area—equivalent to inscribing a triangle of given area in a circle and to Euclid Elements VI.28.

mekos.definition: In Theaetetus's classification (148a–b), any line segment commensurable in linear measure with the chosen unit—specifically the side of an equilateral square number (1, 4, 9, 16, ...).

dynamis.definition: A line segment incommensurable in length (μήκει οὐ σύμμετρος) with the unit, yet commensurable by the plane square area it has the 'power' (δύναται) to generate (√2, √3, √5, ..., √17; cf. Euclid Elements X, Defs. 1–4 & X.9).

isos-isakis.definition: An integer factorable as equal times equal (n = k · k), likened to a square geometric figure; its side is commensurable in length (mēkos) with the unit (Euclid VII, Def. 18).

promekes.definition: An integer enclosed by unequal factors (greater times less, e.g., 3 = 3×1, 6 = 3×2), whose equivalent square has a side that is a quadratic surd (dynamis).

eikasia.definition: Lowest segment (/ A B /) of the Divided Line, directed toward cast shadows and specular reflections in water and polished surfaces.

pistis.definition: Upper segment (/ B C /) of the visible realm on the Divided Line, grasping physical organisms and artifacts—the very objects geometers redeploy as visible diagrams in dianoia (/ C D /) with exact proportional equality ``|BC| = |CD|``.

dianoia.definition: Lower segment (/ C D /) of the intelligible realm: the proper cognitive state of geometry and the sister sciences, reasoning deductively from unexamined hypotheses with the aid of visible diagrams toward immutable intelligible figures.

noesis.definition: Supreme segment (/ D E /) of the Divided Line, treating hypotheses literally as stepping-stones to ascend to the unhypothetical first principle without sensible images.

anhypotheton.definition: The self-grounding first principle of the whole (ἡ τοῦ παντὸς ἀρχή), identified with the Idea of the Good, from which dialectic validates the axioms of mathematics.

arithmetike.definition: First science of the Platonic Quadrivium, contemplating abstract equal units completely indivisible and free of sensible inequality (cf. Euclid Books VII–IX).

logistike.translation: Science of numerical ratios and calculation
logistike.definition: Paired with arithmetic as the study of the mutual quantitative relations of numbers; distinguished into vulgar mercantile reckoning vs. philosophical ratio theory.

stereometria.definition: Third science of the Quadrivium—inserted by Socrates between plane geometry and astronomy—investigating cubes and figures sharing depth; historically realized in Theaetetus's and Eudoxus's work culminating in Euclid Elements Books XI–XIII.

dialektike.translation: Dialectic, coping-stone of the mathematical sciences
dialektike.definition: The synoptic science that grasps the kinship (συγγένεια) and community of the five mathematical disciplines and ascends to the essence (λόγος τῆς οὐσίας) of each thing.

analogia.definition: Continuous equality of ratios (a : b = b : c), revered in Timaeus 31c as the fairest of all bonds because it makes the mean simultaneously first, middle, and last.

desmos.definition: The unifying mathematical relation binding disparate elements into an indissoluble cosmos: one mean for planes (a, ab, b²), two means for solids (a³, a²b, ab², b³).

mesotes.definition: The three classical Archytean means inscribed in Timaeus 31c–36a: geometric √(ab), harmonic 2ab/(a+b) ('exceeding and exceeded by the same fraction of the extremes'), and arithmetic (a+b)/2 ('exceeding and exceeded by an equal number').

epitritos.definition: Superparticular ratio 1 + 1/3 = 4/3 generated between a double-interval baseline a and its harmonic mean 4a/3, as well as between its arithmetic mean 3a/2 and double 2a.

hemiolios.definition: Superparticular ratio 1 + 1/2 = 3/2 generated both in the double intervals (between 1 and 3/2) and throughout the triple intervals (1, 3/2, 2, 3).

epogdoos.definition: Superparticular ratio 1 + 1/8 = 9/8 separating the arithmetic mean (3/2) from the harmonic mean (4/3), used by the Demiurge to measure out every 4:3 fourth.

leimma.definition: The exact rational remainder left when two 9:8 whole tones (81/64) are divided out of a 4:3 fourth: (4/3) / (81/64) = 256/243 ('number to number, 256 to 243').

stoicheion.definition: Originally a letter/syllabic element; transferred by Plato in Timaeus 48b–53d from fire, air, water, and earth (which are 'not even syllables') down to their planar right-triangle constituents—whence Euclid's title Στοιχεῖα.

hemitrigonon.definition: Half of an equilateral triangle bisected by its altitude, having exact side quadrances 1, 3, 4 ('the greater side triple in power of the lesser', 54b5) and rational spreads 1/4, 3/4, 1.

epiprosthesis.definition: Plato's celebrated definition of the straight line (εὐθύ): 'that of which the middle stands in front of (blocks) both extremes' along a visual ray.

tornos-kanon.definition: Canonical constructive instruments generating pure, non-relative geometric beauty (circles, straight lines, planes, and solids) intrinsic to form itself.

symmetros-asymmetros.definition: Having (or lacking) a common unit measure across lengths, surfaces, and solids; declared in Laws VII 819e–820c indispensable knowledge distinguishing rational human beings from 'swine-like' ignorance.
